toolset: The .NET SDK 10.0.402 host (dotnet msbuild), tree on net10.0-windows / net10.0. Counts are unique findings, not log lines (see "note") and are NOT comparable with any baseline generated before 2026-10-18, nor with a Visual Studio MSBuild log - see README.md, "The warning ratchet" and "Retargeting the tree to .NET 10".
note: Maximum allowed occurrences per warning code. Regenerate with warnings.ps1 -UpdateBaseline after an intentional change and record why in notes.<CODE> and the commit message. Codes listed in "untracked" are reported under "informational" instead and never fail the gate.

notes.ASPDEPR008: 4 findings, new with net10: System.Web-era ASP.NET APIs in the HTTP server area. Relevant because the API facade has to be rewritten for Kestrel anyway.
notes.CA1001: 42 findings (44 before the retarget). Two went away with deleted code.
notes.CA1060: 18 findings, unchanged. Top-level statements in files that are not programs.
notes.CA1063: 190 findings (201 before the retarget, 380 and 832 in the two older counting units). The history of this code is a warning about counting: it was 78 on a Visual Studio box with the old rule sets, 832 when severity moved into .editorconfig (every host and every target framework leg reporting), 404 raw log lines once the tree was single-TFM, and 190 unique findings now. None of those jumps was new debt and none of them was fixed.
notes.CA1065: 50 findings, unchanged by the retarget. Properties throwing NotImplementedException - mostly in test mocks.
notes.CA1401: 57 findings, unchanged by the retarget. P/Invoke declarations without AllowSetForegroundWindow-style guards; they move when the Win32 layer moves behind a platform seam.
notes.CA1416: 196 findings, 179 on the same source before the retarget (measured with this same parser in a second git worktree at HEAD, same SDK, same day). The +17 were named exactly: 12 in Source\Main\MediaPortal.Server\MainForm.cs and 5 in ApplicationLauncher.cs, all WinForms members (Application.Run, MessageBox.Show, ListView.*, NotifyIcon.Icon). Those two files contain no new code - MainForm.cs gained four lines (a using and a WFO1000 designer attribute), ApplicationLauncher.cs is untouched - so the newer analyzer simply reports WinForms call sites that .NET 6 kept quiet about. Four findings disappeared, all explained: two in TvdbLib\Cache\BinaryCacheProvider.cs (file deleted with its BinaryFormatter code) and two on PipeAccessRights in Utilities\Process\IpcServer.cs. Treat the 17 as newly *seen*, not new: they are the server's own WinForms UI, which Phase 1 removes anyway. CA1416 remains a proxy only - the real Windows budget is combinedTotalRefs in spine-baseline.json.

notes.CA2213: 45 findings, unchanged. Fields holding disposables that are never disposed.

Re-introducing an obsolete API call is a build failure by design: obsolete means "will break when the platform shrinks", which is what this project is doing.

notes.MSB3270: 0 - kept documented because it was the x86 anchor. The two findings came from MediaPortal.TvEngine.Interfaces/Runtime referencing x86-compiled TV assemblies. The whole TV service layer was deleted on 2026-10-18 together with the last x86-compiled managed dependency. A reappearance means someone referenced an x86 assembly again. notes.NETSDK1138: 1 -> 0. This was "net6.0 is out of support"; the tree now targets net10.0, which is supported until 2028-11-14.

notes.NETSDK1206: 1 finding: a RID-specific warning (win7-x86 style RID handling). See README "What actually pins MP2 to 32-bit".
notes.NU1504: 1 finding: duplicated PackageReference entries in MediaPortal.Mock (System.Data.SQLite.Core listed twice).
notes.NU1510: 20 findings, new with net10: PackageReferences the SDK now provides implicitly (Microsoft.CSharp, System.Drawing.Common, System.Threading.Tasks.Dataflow, ...). Removing them is safe and reduces the audit surface.
notes.NU1701: 20 findings, new with net10 for the same reason: 20 packages only offer .NET Framework assets and are being consumed through the compatibility fallback. They are candidates for replacement or vendoring during Phase 1.
notes.NU1902: 50 findings, and this code simply did not exist on the old tree: NuGet audit is switched on for net8.0+ targets, so the net48/net6.0 legs never evaluated package advisories. The retarget turned on a detector that had been off the whole time and it found 50 packages with known moderate-severity advisories (log4net 2.0.14 GHSA-4p7c..., System.Data.SqlClient 4.8.5 GHSA-98g6..., and friends). This is the single most useful number in this file for Phase 1: the dependency tree has to be modernised before anything ships on Linux. NU1903 (high severity) is reported separately by NuGet and is scored the same way once it appears.
notes.SYSLIB0004: 7 findings, unchanged. Constrained Execution Regions - [MethodImpl] is not supported on .NET.
notes.SYSLIB0006: 2 findings, unchanged. Thread.Abort() - compiles, always throws PlatformNotSupportedException.
notes.SYSLIB0011: BinaryFormatter: 12 findings -> 0, and the code is absent from the file. On .NET 8+ this is an error, not a warning, so the retarget made it impossible to keep: TvdbLib\Cache\BinaryCacheProvider.cs was deleted (its own comment said "broken at the moment -> use CacheProvider") and DiskCachedDictionary now serialises with JsonConvert *without* TypeNameHandling - that option would reintroduce exactly the deserialization gadget risk BinaryFormatter is famous for. If this code reappears, something re-enabled binary deserialization of untrusted data.
notes.SYSLIB0014: 7 findings (6 before). WebRequest/WebClient/ServicePointManager are obsolete and WebRequest.Create is documented as "unsupported" on .NET Core. The sites are OnlineLibraries (CompressionWebClient, FreeDBQuery), ScriptableMetadataExtractor (WebGrabber x3, incl. ServicePointManager), MP2Extended (OnlineVideosManager) and Incubator\MediaServer (XBoxProtocolHandler). They need HttpClient before the media scrapers run anywhere but Windows.
notes.SYSLIB0045: 1 finding, new with net10: a crypto API that .NET 10 marks obsolete (weak crypto; measure before fixing).
notes.SYSLIB0060: 2 findings, new with net10: obsolete ObsoletedException/overload usage surfaced by the newer BCL annotations.
